claims.text: As-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
As-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C and strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
Untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr has poor oxygen resistance at high temperature.
High-temperature oxygen exposure degrades the surface and mechanical properties of untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr.
A conformal 200–300 nm ALD Al2O3 coating will significantly reduce oxygen ingress into as-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr during prolonged high-temperature exposure.
A 200–300 nm ALD Al2O3 coating can preserve the alloy's room-temperature tensile ductility.
A 200–300 nm ALD Al2O3 coating can preserve the alloy's high-temperature yield strength.
Low-temperature atomic layer deposition can produce a thin, dense, uniform, and conformal Al2O3 layer on as-cast HfNbTaTiZr.
The deposited Al2O3 layer will act as a diffusion barrier against oxygen ingress.
The Al2O3 coating will not alter the underlying HfNbTaTiZr microstructure.
Reduced coating thickness and enhanced adhesion will allow the coating to remain intact during high-temperature exposure and mechanical loading.
The thin coating will avoid brittle layers or residual stresses that would compromise alloy ductility or yield strength.
After exposure at 1000 °C in air for 100–500 hours, the coated alloy will have less oxide penetration than uncoated cast HfNbTaTiZr.
After the specified exposure, coated specimens will retain room-temperature tensile ductility within the stated 8–16% baseline range.
At 1000 °C and strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1, coated specimens will retain yield strength within the stated 163–530 MPa baseline range.
The oxidation and mechanical-performance benefits depend on the coating remaining intact during thermal cycling and tensile loading.
Coating cracking or delamination could compromise performance outside the 100–500 hour exposure window or under extreme strain.
